articles.title: Citi on FOMC - FJElite
articles.expand: With our US economics team now expecting a hike at the FOMC’s meeting, we investigate cross asset reactions to the first Fed hikes using high frequency data. Historically, we find that first hikes have not been uniformly bearish on the day, as markets tend to digest much of the tightening risk ahead of start of policy tightening. At first glance, cross-asset reactions at the close on first hikes have been mixed, with US equities rising in four of the seven previous episodes in our sample and no consistent directional response across bonds, gold or FX. articles.title: Goldman Sachs on FOMC - FJElite
articles.expand: BOTTOM LINE We added a 25bp rate hike at this week’s September FOMC meeting to our forecast last Friday following the August CPI report. The report had little impact on our inflation view but pushed market pricing of a hike to nearly 90%, high enough that the FOMC will likely want to avoid the market reaction that would likely follow from remaining on hold. We continue to expect two cuts in 2027 but now expect them in September and December (vs. June and December previously). articles.title: The Riksbank’s Business Survey: “There was some concern before the summer, but then things took a turn for the better”
articles.expand: The economic situation has improved since last spring and, for the first time since September 2022, large Swedish companies’ assessment of the situation is now above its historical average. Before the summer, there were fears that the war in the Middle East would delay the recovery, but those fears have not materialised. Demand has strengthened and the cost increases resulting from the war are considered to be manageable. As a result, companies are taking a more optimistic view of future developments. This is revealed by the Riksbank’s Business Survey in August.
